fact_notes.perfect: A perfect number — equal to the sum of its own divisors. There are only two below a hundred.
fact_notes.factorial: Every number from one to {k}, multiplied. A tidy figure.
fact_notes.primorial: The product of the first {k} primes. Not every age can say that.
fact_notes.square_triangular: Square and triangular at once. The next one is 1225.
fact_notes.power2: A power of two. Computers are fond of these.
fact_notes.cube: A perfect cube. There are only four below a hundred.
fact_notes.square: A perfect square — an age with no rough edges.
fact_notes.fibonacci: A Fibonacci number: the sum of the two before it. This is the sequence things grow along.
fact_notes.triangular: A triangular number — a pyramid {k} rows deep comes to exactly this.
fact_notes.repdigit: Twice the same digit. That happens once in a life, not once a year.
fact_notes.prime: A prime number. It divides by itself and one, and by nothing else.
fact_notes.round: A round number. These are the years people remember.
fact_notes.code: Binary and hexadecimal. Your trade speaks in both.
fact_notes.heart: That is roughly how many times your heart has beaten. Without being asked once.
fact_notes.words: About that many words spoken. A few of them stuck.
fact_notes.orbit: {n} laps around the sun. Without leaving the room.
fact_notes.seasons: That many springs. No two of them alike.
fact_notes.sleep: Roughly that many years asleep. No regrets there.
